## Copy-Edit Log — Analysis-of-Variance

Tracks copy-editing passes over this module's `.qmd` documents. Clear-cut
typos/grammar/spelling errors are corrected directly in the source. Items
that need an author decision (ambiguous phrasing, possible content errors,
incomplete sentences) are left in place but wrapped in `<mark>...</mark>`
so they show up highlighted in the rendered HTML — search the rendered
page or the source for `<mark>` to find them. Line numbers below refer to
`narrative.qmd` as of this pass.

### homework.qmd — 2026-11-16

Rebuilt the homework to `HOMEWORK-DESIGN-GUIDE.md` on the Rice Rivers Center data (daily means, Jan–Mar 2014), replacing the diet-data fill-in version. The worked example is dissolved oxygen ~ Month (+ Tukey, $R^2$) and DO ~ Month × Weather (rain vs dry day); the student task is the same pipeline on river depth. Two Analyze questions: familywise error vs. Tukey, and pseudoreplication / independence from the 15-minute readings. `_homework-key.qmd` rewritten as a full-marks submission.

slides.qmd: the $t$ density slide now defines $x$, $v$ and $\Gamma$. The interaction Tukey plot uses short factor levels (`V`/`Straight`, `Auto`/`Manual`) and horizontal labels; the narrative uses the same levels.

slides.qmd: split the single "Rejection Regions" slide into three slides titled by the null hypothesis ($\mu = c$, $\mu \ge c$, $\mu \le c$), each showing the $t$ distribution ($df = 24$) with its rejection region shaded and the computed cutoff in the caption.

### homework.qmd / in-class.qmd — 2026-11-16

Homework header now requires `execute: echo: false` (research-paper style; `code-tools` still shows the source), with an explanation bullet, a callout above the worked example, and a matching callout in `in-class.qmd`. The worked example and the in-class activity keep their code visible.
